description: Everything that could not be confirmed from an official source, disagreed between sources, or needs a human decision. Nothing here blocks publication; each item is published on the 'Flagged for Review' page. Items FL-001..FL-023 come from the first three sessions and the 074739aa re-audit (05:20Z harvest); FL-024 onward were raised by session-af0789e6's 06:50Z pass and renumbered at merge (original ids kept in 'original_id'). Current 2026-10-22 confidence audit added FL-040 for the withdrawn 65% floor predictions; no bookmaker odds or current OLBG recapture was available.

items.title: Gaelic football is not named in the exclusion list
items.detail: The brief excludes 'football', 'american football' and 'hurling' but never says Gaelic football. Gaelic football is a different sport from association football and from hurling, so it is included here, tagged ambiguous_exclusion=true on every row so the whole block can be dropped with one filter if that was not the intent.

items.title: Kick-off times on OLBG are not labelled with a timezone and are internally inconsistent
items.detail: OLBG prints only 'Today', 'Tomorrow' or a date plus a clock time, never a timezone. Comparing three sports in the same retrieval: snooker 'John Higgins v Jak Jones Today 08:00' matches the official 12:00 UTC start (i.e. US Eastern); greyhound race '11:14 Kinsley' is listed as 06:14 (also US Eastern); but NHL 'PHI Flyers @ BUF Sabres Tomorrow 00:37' cannot be US Eastern, because the official puck-drop is 21 October 19:30 ET. Listed times are therefore recorded as strings only, and no scheduled start in this dataset is derived from them. Where an official start was verified it is stored separately in the 'start' field.

items.title: Same golf tournament shows two different dates/times on OLBG
items.detail: The golf sport page lists 'Genesis Championship — 25 Oct 04:00'. The all-sports page, retrieved minutes earlier, listed the same tournament as 'Tomorrow 02:10'. The official DP World Tour page gives 22-25 October 2026. Only the official dates are published; the OLBG labels are kept verbatim as raw strings.

items.title: NHL fixture labelled 'Tomorrow 00:37' by OLBG; official start is the previous evening
items.detail: OLBG shows PHI Flyers @ BUF Sabres as 'Tomorrow 00:37'. The official start is Wednesday 21 October 2026, 19:30 ET at KeyBank Center. Published start = official time; OLBG label retained as raw text. Same pattern for FLA Panthers @ OTT Senators, whose official start was not independently verified, so that row keeps only the OLBG label.

sources.label: CBS Sports — Sabres vs Flyers, BUF -185, KeyBank Center

items.title: Genesis Championship course par reported as both 71 and 72
items.detail: One preview says 'par-72 course, 7,367 yards', while SBS and the Racing Post say par 71 over 7,367 yards. The official DP World Tour pages retrieved do not state the par. Par is therefore left blank in the dataset rather than picking a side.

items.title: Coverage is the first page of each sport, not the full OLBG card
items.detail: Every sport page paginates behind a 'Load More Tips' control. Only the rows rendered on the first page were captured (137 rows across 15 sports). Fixtures beyond that are not in this dataset, so absence from this list must not be read as 'not happening'.

Our model originates two-way money lines, so the pick is the home side and the draw price is not published.

items.title: Tennis consensus is sometimes not the match winner
items.detail: Zangar Nurlanuly v Tomas Machac shows a '1st Set Winner' consensus, and Bellucci v Etcheverry, Diaz Acosta v Basilashvili and Damm v Cerundolo show 'Set Betting' consensus. None of these is a match-winner pick, so our match probability for those four is originated from the home/away edge only and labelled low confidence.

items.title: Ninety-plus rows are carried by tiny tip samples
items.detail: Many fixtures have one, two or three tips. A 100% confidence figure on a single tip is not evidence, so those rows are capped at low confidence and carry the 'small_sample_lt5_tips' flag. Confidence percentages were copied from OLBG and never recomputed.

items.title: Our handicap and total lines are model assumptions, not market data
items.detail: No bookmaker prices appear in the OLBG pages we retrieved, so handicap and total lines are generated from sport-level dispersion and mean assumptions documented in data/model.md. They are our own lines, which is what was asked for, but they are not verified market quotes and should not be read as such.

items.title: Outright markets have no head-to-head line
items.detail: Golf tournaments, the F1 drivers' championship, the All-Ireland 2027 market, Rugby League futures and greyhound races have fields whose size is not published on the retrieved pages. No price is originated for these; the OLBG consensus selection is shown for reference only and confidence is low.

items.title: Sandbox could not reach OLBG with a normal HTTP client
items.detail: curl to https://www.olbg.com/ returns OpenSSL SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL (exit 35); the same is true for espn.com and bbc.co.uk in this environment. All OLBG pages were therefore retrieved with the agent's page-retrieval tool and transcribed by hand, with the retrieval timestamp stored on every row. A future run with direct HTTP access should re-harvest and diff.

items.title: Re-audit finding on FL-002: OLBG time labels behave like US Eastern
items.detail: Session-074739aa's line-by-line pass compared 40+ OLBG time labels with official start times. Labels sit exactly 6 hours behind France (CET/CEST), 4 hours behind GMT, and match US Eastern clock times for the NHL/NBA/cricket rows (e.g. cricinfo's 11:30 GMT AFG-BAN start is labelled 07:30 on OLBG). The residual oddities (19:10, 19:37, 00:37) look like TV windows or a separate rounding artefact. This does not resolve FL-002 completely - OLBG still publishes no timezone - but the working interpretation is 'US Eastern'. All verified_start values in data/matches.json are the OFFICIAL local times, never OLBG's labels.

items.title: Tiny tip samples and tied splits
items.detail: Most rows carry 1–3 tips. Two NBA money lines (IND@NO, DAL@HOU) are exact 2-2 ties and four handball rows have "Tie" as the most-tipped selection. Our model shrinks every split toward even money; these rows cannot grade above LOW on tips alone.

items.title: Prices, handicaps and totals are model output, not market data
items.detail: OLBG publishes no odds in the retrieved pages. Every price here comes from tools/originate.py (Beta(2,2)-shrunk tip split, home-field logit shift, 5% hold). HIGH picks carry a disclosed 65% probability floor justified only by the official facts quoted in the written prediction. The side rule for non-winner markets and the 0.65 HIGH floor are written up in data/model.md (Step 6).

items.title: Each OLBG list is a server-rendered first page
items.detail: Every sport page ends in a JavaScript "Load More Tips" control the fetcher cannot press. The second harvest found ~40 events the first missed by reading sub-league pages (NBA, European, NHL, Other), and one WTA tie (Fernandez v Sasnovich) present at 05:20Z was no longer rendered at 06:50Z although it has not been played. The list is therefore a sample of OLBG's card, not the whole card. Same mechanism as FL-008 above; the 06:50Z pass added 57 events (sub-league pages) and lost 5 that had started (Fernandez-Sasnovich, Boulter-Golubic, Duckworth-Darderi, Bellucci-Etcheverry, Novara-Marignano), which are therefore no longer on the /olbg board.

items.title: F1 'Win Race' outright was mis-priced as a two-way coin flip (fixed 2026-10-22)

The row stays HIGH (verified, inside -250..+10000, probability 0.284 < 0.70). 'Win Race' is used by no other row, so MTR-913 is the only record that changed; the high/medium/low counts are unchanged. items.title: Seven HIGH write-ups carried stale or wrong figures; corrected against the official source (fixed 2026-10-22)
items.detail: A line-by-line re-read of all 33 published HIGH pieces against the official pages they cite found stale or wrong figures in seven of them; all are corrected and re-sourced. (1) HBL-15 said Szeged had conceded 124 goals in four EHF Champions League games and GOG 132. The official EHF Group D table publishes Szeged 139:136 and GOG 145:139, and the same table plus the EHF round-5 preview show GOG won the reverse fixture 36:34, which the piece had omitted; the write-up was rewritten to those figures and now states the counter-evidence. (2) DRT-11 called Krzysztof Ratajski the 19th seed; the PDC's own field-and-draw release lists him as the third seed against 30th seed Dave Chisnall. (3) MTR-01's headline called Max Verstappen a three-time Austin winner; Formula 1's own race statistics list four Circuit of the Americas wins (2021, 2022, 2023, 2025). (4) TEN-31 gave Alexander Bublik as world No. 22; the official ATP list of 19 October 2026 has him at No. 19. (5) TEN-32 gave Damir Dzumhur as world No. 103; the same list has him at No. 83. (6) TEN-33 said Flavio Cobolli carried 1,650 ATP ranking points; the official list shows 3,640. (7) TEN-27 quoted a '300-point ATP ranking deficit'; the 19 October list puts Vacherot (No. 32, 1,480 points) 415 points and 16 places above Van Assche (No. 48, 1,065). The three tennis values and TEN-27 are ranking-list numbers that moved in the 19 October update, so write-ups drafted against the previous week's list were stale rather than invented; they now cite the dated ATP list. A separate clause in BSB-01 stating that Tampa Bay had not named a Game 1 starter was removed: MLB.com's probable-pitchers page still shows TBD, but multiple reports name Drew Rasmussen, so the claim cannot be published as settled fact. No price, probability or confidence grade changed; every corrected piece remains inside the -250..+10000 band.

items.title: Four more HIGH write-ups corrected after the same line-by-line read (fixed 2026-10-22)
items.detail: The re-read that produced FL-048 also caught four prose claims that were unsupported or wrong. (1) TEN-24 said Alexandra Eala beat Diane Parry 'on Tuesday'; the WTA draw and the tour's own report date that first-round win to Monday 19 October. The same sentence named Ningbo's surface 'Plexipave'; the WTA publishes the event as a hard-court tournament but does not name the acrylic brand, so the brand was removed rather than guessed. (2) TEN-28 described Borna Gojo's two Lyon qualifying wins as 'three-hour battles'; the ATP scorelines (4-6 6-3 7-6(8-6) against Maestrelli and 6-3 7-6(4) against Sachko) do not support a duration, so the phrase now simply says two qualifying wins. The 2-0 Altmaier head-to-head and the 6-3 7-6(2) Fery scoreline in the same piece were both confirmed. (3) GLF-02 said Seamus Power topped the OLBG tournament tips 'ahead of rising contender Ben James'; today's OLBG capture gives Power 5/22 but does not publish James's win-market count, and James is in fact the PGA Tour's +1000/+1175 favourite, so the comparison was dropped and the verifiable 5/22 figure kept. (4) BKB-21's headline called Maccabi's recent home record in the fixture 'perfect'; the EuroLeague game centre says only that the home team won each of the last five meetings, and the most recent meeting was in Madrid, so the headline now states the five-meeting home-side streak exactly. No price, grade or market line changed.

items.title: The OLBG clock is US Eastern, and three same-day HIGH picks had already kicked off at the verification clock (2026-10-22 07:20 UTC)
items.detail: OLBG prints a bare clock with no time zone, and the board previously carried only a resolved calendar date, so a same-day fixture could be published as 'live' hours after its start. Re-reading the organiser pages against the captured labels shows the labels convert only when read as US Eastern (UTC-4): 'Tomorrow 04:00' is NB 13:00 at Almaty (08:00 UTC), 'Tomorrow 08:00' is NB 14:00 at Lyon (12:00 UTC), 'Tomorrow 09:00' is the second match on Brussels' Centre Court, which starts 13:30 local (13:00 UTC), and 'Tomorrow 12:45' / '13:00' are the 18:45 / 19:00 CEST handball throw-offs. At the 07:20 UTC verification clock that means TEN-20 (Ningbo, 05:00 UTC), TEN-21 (Osaka, 05:30 UTC) and CRK-04 (Hagley Oval, 07:00 UTC, ICC live score shows New Zealand 11/0 in the first over) had already started while still published as live HIGH picks. Fix: every row now carries a derived UTC kick-off (board_dates.resolve_kickoff_utc) and a 'started' marker, shown in the board table and on the prediction card. The grade is deliberately not rewritten by the wall clock - the hourly CI rebuild re-derives the board from committed inputs, so a time-dependent grade would make the published result irreproducible; the date-level kick-off gate that archives past-dated picks is unchanged. IRREGULARITY: three HIGH selections were therefore still published after their start; they are now labelled, not hidden.

items.title: TEN-20 published a ranking the official draw contradicts, and TEN-21 cited a page that does not carry its scorelines (fixed 2026-10-22)
items.detail: (1) TEN-20 said Iva Jovic had 'climbed to world No. 12'. The WTA's own Ningbo main-draw sheet, released 21 Oct 2026 22:13, prints Jovic at rank 11 in its PLAYER/RANK column (Rybakina 1, Swiatek 9, Kostyuk 10, Jovic 11, Bencic 12, Shnaider 13, Mertens 14, Cirstea 16). The prose now says No. 11 and cites the sheet. The same sentence's unverifiable 'dropped her to No. 35' for Jasmine Paolini was removed, because Paolini is unseeded at Ningbo and the draw sheet publishes ranks only for seeds; her 6-2, 7-5 first-round win over Anhelina Kalinina is on the sheet and is kept. (2) TEN-21 cited the Osaka player-list page, which does not carry scorelines. The facts in the piece - Siniakova leading Peyton Stearns 6-4, 0-6, 4-0 retired, and Linette beating Claire Liu 6-4, 6-3 - come from the official Osaka main-draw sheet, which is now the cited source. The unverifiable 'world No. 77' tag on Linette was removed for the same reason as Paolini's (unseeded, so no rank is published for her on the sheet), and the Beijing 6-4, 6-3 Siniakova win over Linette was confirmed on the China Open draw sheet and kept. No price, probability or grade changed; both rows stay HIGH and inside the band.

items.title: Five /olbg/ write-ups repeated defects that had already been corrected on the root board
items.detail: A line-by-line read of the live /olbg/ HIGH write-ups against the competitions' own pages found that five of them still carried claims the root board had already been forced to drop, because the two tracks keep separate prediction files. (1) TEN-902110 dated Karen Khachanov's 6-2, 6-4 win over Rei Sakamoto to 'Tuesday's opening round'. The ATP Tour's own Almaty results page places that round-of-32 match on Wednesday 21 October 2026 (its page headers run Tue 20 / Wed 21 / Thu 22 October), so the weekday is corrected to Wednesday. (2) TEN-902071 said Katerina Siniakova booked her last-16 place 'on Tuesday' and (3) TEN-902063 said Ann Li played 'in Osaka on Tuesday'. The WTA's scores and draw pages render results client-side and could not be read in this pass, so those weekdays are no longer asserted at all rather than left standing unchecked. The same applies to TEN-902072, which also repeated the acrylic surface brand the root board removed in FL-049: the WTA publishes Ningbo as a hard-court event without naming a brand, so 'Plexipave' is gone and the piece now says hard courts. (4) GLF-101904 still claimed Seamus Power led the Bermuda tips 'far ahead of any rival ... alongside rising contender Ben James' and that the field was 'confirmed' at 120 players; FL-045 and FL-049 already established that pgatour.com publishes neither a field size nor James's win-market tip count, so the comparison is removed, the field is labelled a disclosed model input, and only the verifiable 5/22 (23%) OLBG share is kept. No price, probability or confidence grade changed in any of the five rows.

items.title: A published audit figure had gone stale and one sentence was no longer true
items.detail: The Flagged for Review page carried the finding 'Seventy of 137 rows had already kicked off when this build ran', with 70 archived rows and 'the remaining 67 rows run from 22 Oct to 25 Jul 2027'. Those three numbers were written when the board held 137 rows; the live board holds 196, so on the 2026-10-22 build the real figures are 74 archived rows and 122 rows still to play. The same finding also said 'a full re-capture and re-verification is the open task recorded in COORDINATION.md', which stopped being true when the 15-sport harvest was completed at 01:26-01:32Z on 22 October. Both were fixed at the source rather than retyped: scripts/build_site.py now computes the archived and live counts from the data on every build, so the published figure can no longer drift from the underlying rows, and the sentence now cites the harvest file that closed the task.
